hook: Ng did more than any single figure to turn machine learning from a graduate-school subject into a skill anyone could learn online, while simultaneously building the industrial-scale infrastructure, Google Brain among it, that made deep learning practical at big-tech scale.
name: Andrew Ng

quote.text: AI is the new electricity. Just as electricity transformed almost everything 100 years ago, today I actually have a hard time thinking of an industry that AI is not going to transform.
quote.context: Widely delivered in talks and interviews from 2017 onward, including his Stanford and Wharton lectures

moniker: AI Educator and Deep Learning Pioneer

reading.body:
Andrew Ng is the single figure most responsible for two things that now reinforce each other: making deep learning infrastructure large enough to matter, and making the skills to use it available to anyone with an internet connection.

The Google Brain co-founding in 2011 was an infrastructure event as much as a research one. It moved deep learning from academic clusters onto the kind of compute that only a company like Google could provision, producing experiments, including the large-scale unsupervised learning work published at ICML 2012, that demonstrated what happened when neural networks met serious hardware. The Baidu role from 2014 to 2017 repeated the pattern at a different industrial scale, applying the same approach to speech recognition and research inside one of the largest technology companies in the world. Both roles connect directly to the thesis that AI capability follows from compute, and compute requires organizations willing to build at scale.

The education work runs parallel and is not separable from the infrastructure story. A Coursera machine learning course without millions of trained practitioners produces little. Practitioners without accessible compute produce little. The data shows Ng operating on both sides, though it does not quantify how many of those practitioners went on to work on the systems the infrastructure side built. What the data does not cover is the content of the research in detail, the internal decisions at Google or Baidu, or how Landing AI's industrial applications have performed. The record here is one of institutional reach across academia, large-scale industry, and mass education, across more than two decades.

quick_facts: Co-founded Google Brain (2011) and served as founding lead of Coursera
Founded and led Baidu's AI Group as Chief Scientist (2014-2017)
Created the Machine Learning course on Coursera, taken by millions
Founded Landing AI, DeepLearning.AI, and the AI Fund

achievements.title: Co-founding Google Brain (2011)
achievements.impact: Built large-scale deep learning infrastructure at Google, including the 'cat-recognizing neural network' experiment that demonstrated unsupervised feature learning at scale.

achievements.title: Stanford CS229 and the Coursera Machine Learning course (2011)
achievements.impact: One of the first and most-enrolled MOOCs in history, credited with introducing machine learning to a global mainstream audience.

achievements.title: Chief Scientist, Baidu (2014-2017)
achievements.impact: Led Baidu's AI Group, expanding speech recognition and deep learning research at one of the world's largest tech companies.

achievements.title: deeplearning.ai and the AI Fund
achievements.impact: Built specialization courses that trained millions of practitioners and funded a portfolio of applied-AI startups.
